correctness.rationale: For even n, central symmetry forces all asymmetries to 1. For odd regular n-gon, side-normal supports at center are r=R*cos(pi/n) outward and R inward, with equal side lengths and sum of side normals zero. For any x inside, t_i=<x,u_i>; the exact cone-volume mass is (r-t_i)/(nr). Guo mu_p^p becomes (nr)^-1 sum (R+t_i)^p (r-t_i)^(1-p). For p=1 the sum equals R/r at every x. For 1<p<infty the summand has strictly positive second derivative p(p-1)(R+r)^2 (R+t)^(p-2)(r-t)^(-p-1); Jensen and sum t_i=0 show lower bound (R/r)^p with equality only if all t_i=0, i.e. x=center. The Minkowski sup endpoint is R/r at center by R/r support bounds; any other center is excluded by the p>1 lower bound and as_p<=as_infty. Jin log endpoint is average log(R/r) on n equal cone-volume atoms. For 0<p<1, the same at-center normalized V_p value is conditional on taking Jin Section 4 proof's V_p convention, NOT an unconditional unambiguous Definition 4.1. Taylor sec(pi/n) expansion is standard. Independent support/Taylor checks odd 3..39 and actual verifier numerical support tests n=3..31 support the exact proof, but do not establish infinitely many n.

Guo et al explicitly ask for classes with as_1=as_infty, which then collapses every intermediate p. The candidate original remainder is the concrete infinite non-centrally-symmetric family of regular odd polygons satisfying equality at sec(pi/n), its log endpoint and interpreted lower-p extension. Jin's accessible text studies log and p mixed-volume asymmetry but not an explicit regular polygon evaluation. The original Guo 2012 primary article could not be retrieved by OA/arXiv routes; authorized Oxford attempt returned VPN disconnected.
